newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore's Goh wants to "move on" with Malaysia.
newsitem.headline: Singapore's Goh wants to "move on" with Malaysia.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong said his country and Malaysia should move beyond the diplomatic row caused by Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew's remarks about Johor, a Straits Times report said on Sunday.
Goh said that Lee had apologised to Malaysians and the Malaysia government and both countries should now concentrate on the positive aspects between them.
"Senior Minister is a member of the Singapore government. He was offside in his remarks on Johor. He recognised he was offside," Goh said.

"He has apologised to Malaysians and the Malaysia government. I would want to move on from here. I do not want to spend too much time looking back, we should try to move forward with the best of our ability," the prime minister told an official dinner at a country club.

Lee, Singapore's prime minister from 1959 to 1990, had said the Malaysian state of Johor was "notorious for shootings, muggings and car-jackings" in a January 27 court affidavit. The affidavit was contained in a libel lawsuit against Singapore opposition politician Tang Liang Hong.
But in a rare public apology on Thursday, Lee said in a statement from his press secretary he had no intention of causing offence and apologised unreservedly for having made the comment.
Despite the apology, some Malaysian politicians and newspapers have continued to criticise Lee.
Goh, commenting on calls for Lee to retract his statement as some thought the apology was inadequate, said it was up to Lee to decide if he wished to do so.
"Senior Minister is a grown man. He decides for himself. We have discussed this, but basically he doesn't retract statements based on perceptions," Goh said.
Lee's apology, made on Thursday after a day of protests in which Malaysian youths hurled insults at him, explained that the remarks were based on perceptions from press reports on Johor.
The minister said that he had not been to Johor, across the causeway from Singapore, since 1990.
Goh added that it was unfortunate that "hiccups" occured in ties between the two countries, but stressed that the fundamentals for the relationship were sound.
